90-94a. Nor from the same place: nor from the same spot. And the phrase οὐ μέν is used for οὐ μήν. For they were separated because of the murder of Phocus, and the one settled in Salamis, which he calls the Attic island, while Peleus settled in Phthia. And by folly, either ignorance or bad counsel.

95-96. And with them from Cecropia: meaning, with these from Attica. For Attica is called Cecropia from Cecrops who was king. And this Teleon is different, the father of Butes, from the one mentioned before (v. 72), the father of Eribotes. And good with the ash spear means warlike, from the ash tree.
from the one mentioned before (v. 72), the father of Eribotes. And good with the ash spear means warlike, from the ash tree.

97-100. Alcon: a proper name, father of Phalerus. Proxenus (fg 5 M. II 462) says that Alcon was the son of Erechtheus. And he says that he fled from Attica with his daughter Chalciope to Euboea, and when his father demanded her back, the Chalcidians did not give her up. And here τηλύγετον does not mean only-begotten, for it is added 'and being alone', but born to him in his old age; for such children are dear.

101-04a. Theseus, who beyond all: Theseus and Pirithous, being of the race, the one from Zeus, the other from Poseidon, made their deeds equal to their lineage. And Theseus, having fallen in love with Helen, had Pirithous as his accomplice, while Pirithous, wishing to marry Persephone, necessarily had Theseus following him. And indeed, having descended through Taenarum and seated themselves on a certain rock, they were unable to rise again. But Heracles, later descending for Cerberus, rescued Theseus as one who had not gone down willingly, but left Pirithous, since he had gone down by his own choice. And the Dioscuri marched against Troezen because of their sister while Theseus was in Hades, and having sacked it, they took captive Aethra, the mother of Theseus.
